newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Power failure hits Karachi's business district.
newsitem.headline: Power failure hits Karachi's business district.

text.p: Prolonged power cuts in this sweltering Pakistani port city halted trading at the Karachi bourse and crippled business activity on Monday, brokers and businessmen said.
Floor brokers at the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) refused to enter the trading hall in protest at the lack of electricity.
"We walked out of the ring because there is no electricity here...The generators of the KSE have also developed some fault," said one broker, Aqeel Suleman.
Dozens of brokers sat on the stairs at the exchange or roamed the parking lot as the building throbbed to the noise of small generators installed at trading offices of KSE members.

"There are more than 600 floor brokers. If we had entered the ring to trade, many would have collapsed because of the heat and poor ventilation," Suleman said. "We will go back to the trading floor when the power supply is restored."
The Karachi Meteorological Department said the temperature had climbed to 35.3 degrees Celsius (95.5 Fahrenheit) by one p.m. (0800 GMT), with 65 percent humidity.
Najam Ali, chief executive of the bourse's Central Depository Company, said it was the sixth or seventh working day in a row that KSE offices had had to use private generators.
A Karachi Electric Supply Corportion (KESC) spokesman blamed a faulty transformer for causing severe power shortages in the main commercial district over the past two weeks or so.

"Its replacement has been delayed because we are short of funds," he said, adding that the outages had become more acute because WAPDA (the state-owned Water and Power Development Authority) had reduced power supplies to the KESC.
The affected area around I.I. Chundrigar Road houses the head offices of most banks, including the State (central) Bank of Pakistan, as well as the stock exchange and business centres.
Cotton dealer Kishan Chand said power was down at the cotton exchange for nearly seven hours at a stretch in working hours.
"I've never experienced such long power cuts in commercial and business centres. I have become ill. How can people increase production and work without elecricity?" he complained.
